body:
## Problem

`ARG XMRIG_VERSION="v6.22.2"` is declared at `Dockerfile:2`, before the first
`FROM`. A Dockerfile ARG declared before the first `FROM` is outside every build
stage. Stage 2 redeclares it (`Dockerfile:24`), so the LABEL works. Stage 1
(`FROM alpine:3.24 AS builder`, line 4) never redeclares it, so `${XMRIG_VERSION}`
on line 12 expands to the empty string.

## Evidence

Empirically confirmed with BuildKit:

```
$ cat Dockerfile
ARG V="v6.22.2"
FROM alpine:3.22 AS builder
RUN echo "stage1 sees: [${V}]" > /out1
ARG V
RUN echo "after redeclare: [${V}]" >> /out1
...
$ docker run --rm argtest
stage1 sees: []
after redeclare: [v6.22.2]
```

So `Dockerfile:12` executes as `git checkout ` with zero arguments. `git checkout`
with no arguments is not an error — confirmed locally:

```
$ git checkout; echo "exit=$?"
exit=0
```

The RUN layer succeeds and the working tree stays on the default branch. Line 19
then builds whatever is at `xmrig/xmrig` master HEAD at build time.

Compounding: `.github/workflows/build.yaml:52-59` passes no `build-args`, so no
value is supplied from CI either.

## Impact

- Every published image is built from an unreviewed upstream master commit, not
  from the audited `v6.22.2` tag. Builds are not reproducible and not pinned —
  an upstream compromise or regression lands in the next tag build silently.
- `org.label-schema.version` (`Dockerfile:32`) reports `v6.22.2` because stage 2
  *does* see the ARG. The label actively lies about the binary's provenance.
- Renovate's `# renovate: ...`-style version bump discipline in the git history
  ("upgrade xmrig to 6.22.2") has had no effect on the artifact since the ARG was
  introduced.

## Fix

Redeclare the ARG inside the builder stage and make the checkout fail loudly:

```dockerfile
ARG XMRIG_VERSION="v6.22.2"

FROM alpine:3.24 AS builder
ARG XMRIG_VERSION

RUN test -n "${XMRIG_VERSION}" && \
  git clone --depth 1 --branch "${XMRIG_VERSION}" \
    https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig.git /xmrig
```

`--branch <tag> --depth 1` removes the `cd`+`checkout` pair entirely (also
clearing hadolint DL3003) and fails the build if the tag does not exist. Also
pass `build-args: XMRIG_VERSION=...` explicitly from the workflow so CI, not the
Dockerfile default, is the single source of truth for the version.

## Resolution
ARG XMRIG_VERSION redeclared inside the builder stage; clone switched to 'git clone --depth 1 --branch $XMRIG_VERSION' with a 'test -n' guard, so an empty value fails the build instead of silently building master. Verified: 'docker run --rm xmrig:ci /bin/xmrig --version' now prints 'XMRig 6.22.2'. CI asserts the running binary matches the Dockerfile ARG.
title: XMRIG_VERSION is empty inside the builder stage; the image builds master HEAD, not the pinned tag

body:
## Problem

`deployment.yaml` overrides the image's CMD with paths from an older image layout
that the current Dockerfile does not produce.

## Evidence

The image, per `Dockerfile:36-41`:

```
mkdir -p /etc/xmrig /log
COPY --from=builder /xmrig/build/xmrig /bin/xmrig
COPY config.json /etc/xmrig/config.json
CMD ["/bin/xmrig", "-c", "/etc/xmrig/config.json"]
```

The Deployment, `deployment.yaml:32-33` and `:41-43`:

```yaml
command: ["/xmrig/xmrig"]
args: ["-c", "/xmrig/etc/config.json"]
volumeMounts:
  - name: config-volume
    mountPath: /xmrig/etc
```

There is no `/xmrig` directory in the final stage at all — `/xmrig` exists only in
the discarded builder stage.

## Impact

The container never starts. kubelet fails to exec `/xmrig/xmrig`
(`exec: "/xmrig/xmrig": stat /xmrig/xmrig: no such file or directory`), the pod
enters CrashLoopBackOff, and the configMap the README instructs users to create is
mounted at a path the binary never reads. The documented Kubernetes path
(README:53-82) is entirely non-functional.

## Fix

Drop the override and let the image's own CMD run, mounting the configMap where
the image expects it:

```yaml
        - image: ivuorinen/docker-xmrig:latest
          name: xmrig
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config-volume
              mountPath: /etc/xmrig
```

A configMap mounted at `/etc/xmrig` from `--from-file config.json` produces
`/etc/xmrig/config.json`, which matches the image CMD. Remove the `command:`/`args:`
keys so the image contract is the only definition of how xmrig is launched.

## Resolution
Removed the command/args override and moved the configMap mount to /etc/xmrig, so the image's own CMD is the contract. Verified equivalent container (uid 10001, read-only rootfs, all caps dropped, config bind-mounted ro at /etc/xmrig) starts and stays healthy.
title: Kubernetes Deployment invokes /xmrig/xmrig and mounts config at /xmrig/etc; neither path exists in the image

body:
## Problem

The primary "How to use this image" example invokes a binary and a config path
that the image does not contain.

## Evidence

`README.md:39-44`:

```bash
docker run -dit --rm \
    --volume "$(pwd)"/config.json:/xmrig/etc/config.json:ro \
    --volume "$(pwd)"/log:/xmrig/log \
    --name xmrig ivuorinen/docker-xmrig:latest \
    /xmrig/xmrig --config=/xmrig/etc/config.json
```

The image provides `/bin/xmrig` and `/etc/xmrig/config.json` (`Dockerfile:38-41`).
`/xmrig` does not exist in the final stage.

Two further defects in the same four lines:
- `:ro` on the config mount conflicts with `"autosave": true` (`config.json:2`);
  xmrig will try to rewrite the file and fail.
- `/xmrig/log` is not where the shipped config writes. `config.json:32` sets
  `"log-file": "/log/xmrig.log"`, and `Dockerfile:36` creates `/log`.

## Impact

Every user following the README's first deployment path gets an immediate
`no such file or directory` exec failure. This is the repository's headline
example and it is also the Docker Hub description (pushed by the
`update_description` job in `.github/workflows/build.yaml:105-118`), so the broken
command is the public-facing documentation for the image.

## Fix

Replace the example with one that matches the image contract and drops the
redundant command override:

```bash
docker run -dit --rm \
    --volume "$(pwd)"/config.json:/etc/xmrig/config.json \
    --volume "$(pwd)"/log:/log \
    --name xmrig ivuorinen/docker-xmrig:latest
```

Then update the "Persistent logging" section (README:98-114), which currently
tells the user to set `"log-file": "/xmrig/log/xmrig.log"` — also wrong — to
`/log/xmrig.log`.

## Resolution
docker run example now uses /etc/xmrig/config.json and /log and drops the command override; added an 'Image layout' table so the paths are stated once. Persistent-logging snippet corrected to /log/xmrig.log.
title: README docker run example uses image paths that do not exist; the documented quickstart cannot work

body:
## Problem

The reference `docker-compose.yml` silently adds a second service that grants a
container root-equivalent control of the host and auto-replaces the miner image
from an unpinned tag.

## Evidence

`docker-compose.yml:11-14`:

```yaml
  watchtower:
    image: containrrr/watchtower
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
```

- No tag → `containrrr/watchtower:latest`, resolved fresh on every `docker compose pull`.
- `/var/run/docker.sock` mounted read-write. Anything that can talk to that socket
  can `docker run -v /:/host --privileged`, i.e. it is host root.
- Watchtower is not mentioned anywhere in `README.md`. A user who follows
  README:46-51 (`docker-compose up -d`) gets it without being told.

## Impact

A compromise of either the Watchtower image or the `ivuorinen/docker-xmrig:latest`
tag on Docker Hub escalates directly to host root: Watchtower polls Docker Hub,
pulls whatever `:latest` now points to, and restarts the miner with it — no human
in the loop. This is the classic supply-chain-to-host-root path, and it is enabled
by default in the file the README tells users to run.

## Fix

Remove the `watchtower` service from the reference compose file. Auto-update is a
deployment policy, not part of a miner image's reference manifest, and the README
never claims it.

If it must stay, it belongs behind an opt-in profile, pinned, and read-only:

```yaml
  watchtower:
    image: containrrr/watchtower:1.7.1
    profiles: ["autoupdate"]
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    restart: unless-stopped
```

and the README must document that `--profile autoupdate` grants a container
host-root-equivalent access.

## Resolution
Watchtower service removed from docker-compose.yml entirely, taking the /var/run/docker.sock mount and the unpinned :latest auto-update with it.
title: docker-compose ships an undocumented Watchtower with the Docker socket mounted and an unpinned :latest image

body:
## Problem

The builder stage adds the Alpine *edge* rolling repository on top of a pinned
Alpine 3.24 base, then installs all build dependencies with no version pins.

## Evidence

`Dockerfile:7-8`:

```dockerfile
RUN echo 'https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/edge/community' >> /etc/apk/repositories && \
  apk --no-cache add git build-base linux-headers cmake libuv-dev openssl-dev hwloc-dev gcompat
```

`apk` resolves each package against the union of the 3.24 repos and edge, and
prefers the highest version — which for most of these is the edge one. Every
package here (`git`, `build-base`, `cmake`, `libuv-dev`, `openssl-dev`,
`hwloc-dev`, `gcompat`) exists in Alpine 3.24 `main` or `community`; nothing in
the list requires edge.

hadolint agrees on the pinning half: `Dockerfile:7 DL3018 warning: Pin versions in apk add`.

The runtime stage (`Dockerfile:34`) does *not* add edge, so it links against 3.24
`libuv` and `hwloc` while the binary was compiled against edge headers of the same
libraries. That is an unchecked ABI mismatch between build and runtime.

## Impact

- Two builds of the same git tag produce different binaries. Combined with the
  empty-`XMRIG_VERSION` defect, nothing about the published artifact is pinned.
- An edge `libuv`/`hwloc`/`openssl` soname bump breaks the runtime stage with a
  loader error at container start, and the CI pipeline has no step that would
  catch it (the image is pushed without ever being run).
- Renovate cannot see or bump anything installed from edge.

## Fix

Delete the edge repository line. Everything needed is in 3.24:

```dockerfile
RUN apk --no-cache add git build-base linux-headers cmake \
      libuv-dev openssl-dev hwloc-dev
```

If a specific package genuinely needs edge later, add it with an explicit
`--repository=.../edge/community` scoped to that one package rather than
globally re-pointing apk.

## Resolution
Dropped the edge/community repository line. Verified all build deps (git build-base linux-headers cmake libuv-dev openssl-dev hwloc-dev) and runtime deps (libuv hwloc) resolve from Alpine 3.24 alone via 'apk add --simulate', and the full image builds and runs.
title: Alpine edge/community is appended to a 3.24 base, making every build unpinned and non-reproducible

body:
## Problem

The build patches XMRig's source and distributes the resulting binary on Docker
Hub. XMRig is GPL-3.0. The repository declares MIT and does not disclose the
modification or offer the corresponding source of the modified work.

## Evidence

The modification, `Dockerfile:15`:

```dockerfile
RUN sed -i 's/1;/0;/g' /xmrig/src/donate.h
```

Distribution, `.github/workflows/build.yaml:52-59` and `:96-100` — the built
binary is pushed to `ivuorinen/docker-xmrig` on Docker Hub.

`LICENSE` is MIT, "Copyright (c) 2024 Ismo Vuorinen", with no GPL text and no
exception carve-out.

`README.md:123` states: "The Docker image is licensed under the terms of the MIT
License. XMRig is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0." The first
clause is inaccurate — the image *contains* a modified GPLv3 binary, so the image
as a distributed whole cannot be MIT.

Nothing in the repository states that donate.h was altered, and there is no
`NOTICE`, no `COPYING`, no written offer, and no copy of the GPL-3.0 text shipped
in the image or the repo.

## Impact

GPL-3.0 §5(a) requires modified works to "carry prominent notices stating that you
modified it, and giving a relevant date". §6 requires that conveying the object
form be accompanied by the corresponding source or a written offer. Neither is
satisfied. Every published image tag is a distribution that does not meet the
license's conditions, and the README's MIT claim misleads downstream users about
what they may do with the image.

## Fix

Three concrete changes:

1. Add a `NOTICE` file at the repo root stating the modification explicitly:
   `"This image contains XMRig (https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig), licensed
   GPL-3.0-or-later, modified: src/donate.h patched to set the donate level to 0.
   Modified <date>."`
2. Ship the GPL text and the modification in the image so the binary travels with
   its source obligation:
   ```dockerfile
   COPY --from=builder /xmrig/LICENSE /usr/share/licenses/xmrig/LICENSE
   COPY --from=builder /xmrig/src/donate.h /usr/share/licenses/xmrig/donate.h
   ```
   plus a `--build-arg`-free note pointing at this repo's Dockerfile as the build
   recipe.
3. Correct `README.md:123` to say the *packaging in this repository* (Dockerfile,
   manifests, docs) is MIT, while the distributed image contains GPL-3.0 XMRig and
   is therefore conveyed under GPL-3.0.

## Resolution
Added NOTICE at the repo root stating the donate.h modification and the GPL-3.0 conveyance; image now ships /usr/share/licenses/xmrig/{LICENSE,donate.h,NOTICE}; README license section corrected to say the packaging is MIT but the image is GPL-3.0-or-later. Verified the three files are present in the built image.
title: Image ships a modified GPL-3.0 binary while the repository declares MIT, with no modification notice and no corresponding-source offer

body:
## Problem

The release pipeline builds, pushes, and publishes a manifest list without a
single step that executes the binary it just shipped.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/build.yaml` job graph is `build` → `merge` → `update_description`.
The only step resembling verification is `:101-103`:

```yaml
      - name: Inspect image
        run: |
          docker buildx imagetools inspect ${{ env.REGISTRY_IMAGE }}:${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}
```

`imagetools inspect` reads the registry manifest. It does not pull layers, does
not start a container, and does not exercise the binary. There is no
`docker run`, no `--version` check, no Trivy/Grype scan, no hadolint step, and no
test job of any kind in the repository.

The `build` job also pushes with `push=true` (`:59`) *before* anything could gate
it — the artifact is public the moment the build layer succeeds.

## Impact

Every defect in this audit that manifests at runtime ships undetected:
- the empty `XMRIG_VERSION` producing a master-HEAD binary,
- a potential edge-vs-3.24 shared-library ABI break at container start,
- a silently no-op `sed` leaving upstream's 1% donate level enabled.

A single `docker run --rm <image> --version` in the `build` job would have caught
the first and third of those, and any loader breakage from the second.

## Fix

Add a gating smoke test to the `build` job, between build and the manifest merge.
Build to a local tag first, verify, then push:

```yaml
      - name: Build for test
        uses: docker/build-push-action@<pinned>
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: ${{ matrix.platform }}
          load: true
          tags: test-image
          build-args: XMRIG_VERSION=${{ env.XMRIG_VERSION }}
      - name: Smoke test
        run: |
          out=$(docker run --rm test-image /bin/xmrig --version)
          echo "$out"
          echo "$out" | grep -q "${XMRIG_VERSION#v}"   # fails if the tag was not honoured
```

Add `trivy image --exit-code 1 --severity CRITICAL,HIGH test-image` alongside it,
and `hadolint Dockerfile` + `actionlint` as a cheap lint job. All are gating —
`continue-on-error` would defeat the purpose.

## Resolution
Added gating lint + verify jobs. verify builds amd64 with load:true, runs the binary, asserts its version equals the Dockerfile ARG, and runs trivy with exit-code 1 on CRITICAL/HIGH. build/merge now need verify, so a failed smoke test blocks the manifest list.
title: CI pushes to Docker Hub without ever running the built image; no smoke test and no image scan

body:
## Problem

Three files disagree on where xmrig writes its log, so the bind mount that is
supposed to persist logs captures nothing.

## Evidence

Four separate paths for one file:

| Location | Path |
| --- | --- |
| `config.json:32` | `"log-file": "/log/xmrig.log"` |
| `Dockerfile:36` | `mkdir -p /etc/xmrig /log` |
| `docker-compose.yml:9` | `./log:/xmrig/log:rw` |
| `README.md:41` and `README.md:105` | `/xmrig/log` and `"log-file": "/xmrig/log/xmrig.log"` |

The image creates `/log` and the shipped config writes to `/log/xmrig.log`.
The compose file mounts the host `./log` over `/xmrig/log` — a directory the
image does not create and the config never touches.

## Impact

`docker compose up -d` produces a running miner whose log accumulates inside the
container's writable layer at `/log/xmrig.log` and is destroyed with the container.
The host `./log` directory stays empty forever. The README section titled
"Persistent logging" (`README.md:98-114`) documents exactly this workflow as
working, so the failure is silent — the user sees an empty directory and no error.

Because the container's writable layer is unbounded, the log also grows without
rotation until it fills the Docker storage driver's filesystem (see the separate
log-rotation finding).

## Fix

Make `/log` the single path everywhere. In `docker-compose.yml:9`:

```yaml
      - ./log:/log:rw
```

In `README.md:41` change the second `--volume` to `"$(pwd)"/log:/log`, and in
`README.md:105` change the snippet to `"log-file": "/log/xmrig.log"`. Leave
`config.json:32` and `Dockerfile:36` as they are — they are the two that already
agree.

## Resolution
All four locations now agree on /log: compose mounts ./log:/log, README docker run uses /log, README snippet says /log/xmrig.log. Verified xmrig writes /log/xmrig.log as uid 10001 in both a normal container and a read-only-rootfs container.
title: Log file path in config.json matches neither the compose mount nor the README; container logs never reach the host

body:
## Problem

Nothing in the repository constrains the miner's privileges. It runs as uid 0 in
Docker, in Compose, and in Kubernetes.

## Evidence

- `Dockerfile` has no `USER` instruction; the final `CMD` (`:41`) therefore runs
  as root. Three independent scanners agree:
  - trivy `DS-0002 (HIGH)`: "Specify at least 1 USER command in Dockerfile with non-root user as argument"
  - checkov `CKV_DOCKER_3`
  - semgrep `dockerfile.security.missing-user.missing-user` at `Dockerfile:41`
- `deployment.yaml` has no `securityContext` at pod or container level
  (`:29-43`). trivy/checkov/semgrep flag: `KSV-0012`/`CKV_K8S_23` runAsNonRoot,
  `KSV-0001`/`CKV_K8S_20` allowPrivilegeEscalation, `KSV-0014`/`CKV_K8S_22`
  readOnlyRootFilesystem, `KSV-0003`/`KSV-0004`/`CKV_K8S_37` capabilities.drop,
  `CKV_K8S_31` seccompProfile, `CKV_K8S_38` automountServiceAccountToken.
- `docker-compose.yml:2-10` sets no `user:`, `cap_drop:`, `read_only:`, or
  `security_opt:`.

xmrig needs no root privileges for its default configuration path. The only
options that would want elevated access are the MSR/hugepage settings in
`config.json` (see the separate finding on those), and those are already
non-functional in an unprivileged container.

## Impact

Any remote-code-execution in xmrig's pool-protocol parsing — the process's one
network-facing attack surface, speaking a plaintext line protocol to an
attacker-influenced pool (`"tls": {"enabled": false}`, `config.json:49-51`) —
lands as uid 0 with a writable root filesystem and the default capability set.
Under Compose it lands next to a container that has the Docker socket.

## Fix

In the Dockerfile, create and switch to an unprivileged user, and give it the log
directory:

```dockerfile
RUN apk --no-cache add libuv hwloc && \
  mkdir -p /etc/xmrig /log && \
  adduser -S -u 10001 -h /log xmrig && \
  chown xmrig /log

COPY --from=builder /xmrig/build/xmrig /bin/xmrig
COPY config.json /etc/xmrig/config.json
USER 10001
CMD ["/bin/xmrig", "-c", "/etc/xmrig/config.json"]
```

In `deployment.yaml`, add the matching context:

```yaml
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
        seccompProfile: { type: RuntimeDefault }
      containers:
        - name: xmrig
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }
```

`readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` requires an `emptyDir` at `/log` and
`"autosave": false` in the config, since xmrig otherwise rewrites its config file.

## Resolution
Dockerfile creates uid 10001 and sets USER 10001; deployment.yaml gained pod securityContext (runAsNonRoot, runAsUser/fsGroup 10001, seccompProfile RuntimeDefault), container securityContext (allowPrivilegeEscalation false, readOnlyRootFilesystem true, capabilities drop ALL) and automountServiceAccountToken false. Verified: 'id' reports uid=10001, and the container runs clean with --read-only --cap-drop ALL. semgrep 3 findings -> 0; checkov dockerfile 2 failures -> 0.
title: Container runs as root everywhere: no USER, no securityContext, no capability drop, writable root filesystem

body:
## Problem

Donation is disabled by rewriting upstream source with an unanchored global
substitution, and nothing checks that the substitution matched.

## Evidence

`Dockerfile:15`:

```dockerfile
RUN sed -i 's/1;/0;/g' /xmrig/src/donate.h
```

The target file at `v6.22.2` is:

```c
#ifndef XMRIG_DONATE_H
#define XMRIG_DONATE_H
constexpr const int kDefaultDonateLevel = 1;
constexpr const int kMinimumDonateLevel = 1;
#endif // XMRIG_DONATE_H
```

The pattern happens to match today. It is unanchored, matches any `1;` anywhere in
the file, and `sed` exits 0 whether or not it replaced anything. If upstream
changes the literal to `1u;`, `1 ;`, `0x1;`, moves the constants to another file,
or renames the header, the RUN still succeeds and the build produces a binary with
`kMinimumDonateLevel = 1`.

This matters more than usual because `config.json:33-34` sets
`"donate-level": 0` — xmrig clamps that value to `kMinimumDonateLevel` at runtime,
so the config setting is *only* effective if the sed worked. There is no CI step
that runs the image (see the CI smoke-test finding), so a silent no-op is
undetectable from the outside.

## Impact

A future upstream refactor silently re-enables 1% donation mining on every
deployment of this image, with the config file still claiming
`"donate-level": 0`. The failure is invisible: no build error, no log line, no
test.

## Fix

Target the constants precisely and fail the build if either does not match:

```dockerfile
RUN sed -i -E 's/^(constexpr const int kDefaultDonateLevel) = [0-9]+;/\1 = 0;/' /xmrig/src/donate.h && \
    sed -i -E 's/^(constexpr const int kMinimumDonateLevel) = [0-9]+;/\1 = 0;/' /xmrig/src/donate.h && \
    grep -q 'kDefaultDonateLevel = 0;' /xmrig/src/donate.h && \
    grep -q 'kMinimumDonateLevel = 0;' /xmrig/src/donate.h
```

The two `grep -q` guards turn a silent no-op into a build failure.

## Resolution
Replaced the blanket 's/1;/0;/g' with two anchored -E substitutions on the named constants plus two 'grep -q' guards, so a no-op fails the build. Verified in the built image: donate.h shows both constants = 0 and the miner's own startup banner reports 'DONATE 0%'.
title: The donate.h patch is an unverified blanket regex; a silent no-op re-enables upstream donation

body:
## Problem

The shipped configuration points at a hostname that exists only on the author's
LAN, and the README's description of the default behaviour is wrong.

## Evidence

`config.json:35-42`:

```json
  "pools": [
    {
      "url": "tunkki:3333",
      "user": "${HOSTNAME}",
      "pass": "",
      "keepalive": true
    }
  ]
```

`tunkki` is a bare single-label hostname with no domain — resolvable only inside
one network. Combined with `config.json:46-47` (`"retries": 5`,
`"retry-pause": 5`) and `docker-compose.yml:10` (`restart: unless-stopped`), the
container fails DNS resolution, retries, exits, and is restarted forever.

The README describes different behaviour at `README.md:68-69`:

> _remember to edit this file with your own pool configuration and wallet address
> or it will mine against my anonymised docker wallet_

It will not mine against anything — it cannot resolve the host. The README also
never mentions `tunkki` or that the default is a private address.

## Impact

The default experience for anyone cloning this repository is a restart loop with
no successful mining and no explanation in the docs. The README's claim that the
default mines to the author's wallet sends users looking for the wrong problem.

## Fix

Make the placeholder obviously a placeholder, and align the README:

```json
      "url": "CHANGE-ME.example:3333",
```

and replace `README.md:68-69` with a statement of fact: "the shipped `config.json`
contains a placeholder pool address and will not connect until you replace
`pools[0].url` with your own pool or p2pool node."

Note `"user": "${HOSTNAME}"` is correct and needs no change — xmrig expands it via
`src/base/io/Env.cpp:62-64`, which registers `HOSTNAME` as a built-in variable
defaulting to `gethostname()`.

## Resolution
Pool url is now the obvious placeholder CHANGE-ME.example:3333; README states up front that it will not connect until replaced, and the false 'mines against my anonymised docker wallet' claim is gone. Confirmed the 'user': '${HOSTNAME}' field was correct and left unchanged.
title: Default pool host 'tunkki:3333' is the author's private hostname; out of the box the miner cannot connect

## Problem

No job or workflow in `.github/workflows/build.yaml` sets `permissions:`, so every
job's `GITHUB_TOKEN` inherits whatever the repository/organization default is —
historically `write-all` for repositories created before the default changed.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/build.yaml` has three jobs (`build:23`, `merge:73`,
`update_description:105`) and no `permissions:` key anywhere in the file.
checkov flags this as `CKV2_GHA_1: "Ensure top-level permissions are not set to write-all"`.

None of the three jobs needs any repository write access:
- `build` checks out, builds, and pushes to Docker Hub using
  `secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` (`:50-51`) — not `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- `merge` never checks out at all; it only talks to Docker Hub.
- `update_description` checks out and calls Docker Hub's API.

## Impact

Every step in the pipeline — including three third-party actions and the
`docker/build-push-action` build, which executes the repository's own Dockerfile —
runs with a token that may be able to push commits, create releases, and alter
workflows. A compromised action version or a malicious PR-authored Dockerfile
change would inherit that. The blast radius is unnecessary: the pipeline's real
credential is the Docker Hub token, and the GitHub token is only needed for
`actions/checkout` to read.

## Fix

Add a least-privilege default at the top of the file, below `env:`:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
```

That covers `actions/checkout` in `build` and `update_description`, and `merge`
needs nothing at all — set `permissions: {}` on that job explicitly.

## Resolution
Added workflow-level 'permissions: contents: read'. checkov github_actions failures 1 -> 0.
title: Workflow declares no permissions block, so GITHUB_TOKEN gets the repository default scope

body:
## Problem

`"autosave": true` makes xmrig write the config file back on change, but the
repository's two deployment examples mount that file with opposite intentions and
neither is right.

## Evidence

`config.json:2`: `"autosave": true`, together with `config.json:54`: `"watch": true`.

- `docker-compose.yml:8` mounts `./config.json:/etc/xmrig/config.json:rw` — xmrig
  will rewrite the user's checked-out `config.json` in place, normalising it and
  adding every default key. The user's file changes under them, and `git status`
  in the cloned repo goes dirty.
- `README.md:40` mounts the same file `:ro` — xmrig's autosave write fails. The
  `"watch": true` reload loop then re-reads a file it cannot rewrite.
- `deployment.yaml:41-43` mounts it from a configMap, which is always read-only in
  Kubernetes, so autosave cannot work there either.

## Impact

Two of three documented deployment paths hit a write failure on a file the miner
believes it owns; the third silently mutates a file that is under version control
in the user's clone. None of this is documented anywhere in the README.

## Fix

Turn autosave off — it has no benefit for a container whose config is supplied by
the operator:

```json
  "autosave": false,
```

Then `docker-compose.yml:8` can safely become `:ro`, matching the README and the
Kubernetes configMap, and all three paths behave identically. Keep
`"watch": true` if live config reload is wanted; it works fine read-only.

## Resolution
Set autosave:false, so read-only mounts are correct everywhere; compose config mount changed to :ro to match the README and the Kubernetes configMap. Verified the miner runs with the config bind-mounted read-only.
title: autosave rewrites the user's bind-mounted config; the README's :ro example makes that a runtime error

body:
## Problem

The shipped configuration enables four options that require host-level privileges
the container is never granted, in any of the three documented deployment paths.

## Evidence

`config.json:6-21`:

```json
  "randomx": {
    "1gb-pages": true,
    "rdmsr": true,
    "wrmsr": true,
    "cache_qos": true,
    ...
  },
  "cpu": {
    "huge-pages": true,
```

What each needs:
- `rdmsr`/`wrmsr` — read/write x86 model-specific registers via `/dev/cpu/*/msr`,
  requiring the host `msr` kernel module plus `CAP_SYS_RAWIO` and a device mount.
- `cache_qos` — Intel CAT/RDT, same MSR path.
- `1gb-pages` — the host booted with `hugepagesz=1G` *and* the container given
  the hugepage allocation.
- `huge-pages` — 2 MB hugepages, needs `vm.nr_hugepages` on the host and
  `CAP_IPC_LOCK` in the container.

None of `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, or `deployment.yaml` grants any
capability, device, or hugepage resource. `deployment.yaml:34-40` requests plain
`memory`/`cpu` only. `rdmsr`/`wrmsr` are additionally x86-only, while the CI
builds and the README (`README.md:73`, "Turing Pi cluster") target `linux/arm64`.

## Impact

Every one of these silently falls back at startup — xmrig logs a warning and
continues at reduced hashrate. The user gets a config that reads as
performance-tuned but delivers none of it, with no note anywhere explaining why
or what the host would need to provide. On the arm64 images the MSR options are
meaningless outright.

## Fix

Set the container-appropriate defaults in `config.json` and document the opt-in:

```json
  "randomx": {
    "init": -1,
    "init-avx2": -1,
    "mode": "auto",
    "1gb-pages": false,
    "rdmsr": false,
    "wrmsr": false,
    "cache_qos": false,
    "numa": true,
    "scratchpad_prefetch_mode": 1
  },
```

Add a README subsection stating that MSR tuning requires
`--cap-add SYS_RAWIO --device /dev/cpu` on an x86 host with the `msr` module
loaded, and that hugepages require host `vm.nr_hugepages` plus `--cap-add IPC_LOCK`
— so a user who wants the hashrate knows exactly what to grant.

## Resolution
randomx 1gb-pages/rdmsr/wrmsr/cache_qos all set false; cpu.huge-pages left true because it degrades gracefully. Added a README 'Performance tuning' table naming exactly what each option requires to be re-enabled. Verified the startup banner reports '1GB PAGES disabled' with no errors.
title: RandomX config requests MSR and 1 GB hugepage privileges that an unprivileged container cannot have; degradation is silent and undocumented

body:
## Problem

Two build arguments exist solely to populate OCI-style labels, and the pipeline
never passes either one.

## Evidence

`Dockerfile:24-32`:

```dockerfile
ARG XMRIG_VERSION
ARG BUILD_DATE
ARG VCS_REF

LABEL org.label-schema.schema-version="1.0" \
  org.label-schema.build-date=$BUILD_DATE \
  org.label-schema.vcs-url="https://github.com/ivuorinen/docker-xmrig" \
  org.label-schema.vcs-ref=$VCS_REF \
  org.label-schema.version=${XMRIG_VERSION}
```

`.github/workflows/build.yaml:52-59` is the only place the image is built and has
no `build-args:` input:

```yaml
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@...
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: ${{ matrix.platform }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          outputs: type=image,...
```

`BUILD_DATE` and `VCS_REF` have no defaults, so they expand to empty and the
image carries `org.label-schema.build-date=""` and `org.label-schema.vcs-ref=""`.

## Impact

Dead configuration that reads as working provenance metadata. Anyone inspecting
the image for a build date or source commit gets empty strings. The
`org.label-schema.*` namespace is also deprecated in favour of `org.opencontainers.image.*`,
and `docker/metadata-action` (`:38-42`) already emits the correct OCI labels via
`steps.meta.outputs.labels`, which the build *does* apply — so these hand-rolled
labels are both broken and redundant with a working mechanism in the same file.

## Fix

Delete the `BUILD_DATE`/`VCS_REF` ARGs and the entire `LABEL` block. The
`labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}` line already supplies
`org.opencontainers.image.created`, `.revision`, `.source`, and `.version`
correctly. Keep only the one label metadata-action cannot know — the upstream
miner version:

```dockerfile
ARG XMRIG_VERSION
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.version=${XMRIG_VERSION}
```

and pass `build-args: XMRIG_VERSION=...` from the workflow (also required by the
builder-stage ARG finding).

## Resolution
Deleted the BUILD_DATE/VCS_REF ARGs and the whole org.label-schema LABEL block; docker/metadata-action already supplies the OCI labels. Kept org.opencontainers.image.version from the (now correctly scoped) XMRIG_VERSION ARG, plus an explicit licenses label. No build-args needed: the Dockerfile ARG is the single source and CI asserts against it.
title: BUILD_DATE and VCS_REF build args are declared and labelled but never supplied; the labels ship empty

body:
## Problem

The `push` trigger is filtered to tags only, but also carries a `paths-ignore`
list written for branch pushes. One entry does not match any file in the repo,
and the combination can suppress a release build entirely.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/build.yaml:3-13`:

```yaml
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    paths-ignore:
      - ".github/**"
      - "LICENSE"
      - ".editorconfig"
      - "deployment.yaml"
      - "renovate.json"
    tags:
      - "*"
```

Concrete problems:

1. `renovate.json` matches nothing. The file is at `.github/renovate.json`
   (already covered by `.github/**`). The bare path is dead config.
2. With `tags:` and no `branches:`, pushes to `main` never trigger this workflow.
   The repository has no other workflow — `.github/workflows/` contains only
   `build.yaml`. So no push to `main` ever builds the Dockerfile, and there is no
   `pull_request` trigger either. Every change to `Dockerfile` or `config.json`
   reaches a release tag having never been built once.
3. A release tag placed on a commit whose diff touches only the ignored paths can
   be filtered out, producing a tag with no published image and no failure signal.

## Impact

The 55-commit history is dominated by Renovate dependency bumps to the Dockerfile
base image and the actions themselves. None of those PRs was ever built or tested
by CI — the first execution of a bumped Dockerfile is the release build that
pushes it to Docker Hub with `push=true` (`:59`). This is how the empty-`XMRIG_VERSION`
defect and the `/xmrig/xmrig` path drift survived unnoticed across many releases.

## Fix

Split the two concerns. Build-and-verify on every change, publish only on tags:

```yaml
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ["*"]
```

Drop the `paths-ignore` block — it saves nothing meaningful on a repository this
size and its only effect here is to create the silent-no-release hazard. Gate the
push step instead:

```yaml
          outputs: type=image,name=${{ env.REGISTRY_IMAGE }},push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') }}
```

and add `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')` to the `merge` job, so PR and
main builds validate without publishing.

## Resolution
Trigger is now workflow_dispatch + pull_request + push on branches:[main] and tags:[*], with the whole paths-ignore block (including the dead 'renovate.json' entry) removed. Publishing is gated on 'if: startsWith(github.ref, refs/tags/)' on the build job, so PRs and main builds verify without pushing.
title: Trigger runs only on tag pushes while carrying a paths-ignore list; nothing validates the Dockerfile before a release tag is cut

body:
## Problem

The Compose reference deployment has no resource constraints, while the
Kubernetes manifest for the same workload does.

## Evidence

`docker-compose.yml:2-10` in full:

```yaml
  xmrig:
    image: ivuorinen/docker-xmrig:latest
    container_name: xmrig
    volumes:
      - ./config.json:/etc/xmrig/config.json:rw
      - ./log:/xmrig/log:rw
    restart: unless-stopped
```

No `deploy.resources.limits`, no `cpus:`, no `mem_limit:`, no `cpuset:`.
`config.json:17-20` enables the CPU backend with no `max-threads-hint` and no
`threads` array, so xmrig auto-detects and uses every available core.
`config.json:55-56` sets `"pause-on-battery": false` and `"pause-on-active": false`,
removing the two conditions under which xmrig would back off on its own.

By contrast `deployment.yaml:34-40` does set `limits: {memory: 2Gi, cpu: "1"}` for
the identical workload — the two reference manifests disagree by a factor of the
host's core count.

## Impact

`docker compose up -d`, the command the README gives at `README.md:46-51`, pins
every core of the host at 100% indefinitely with `restart: unless-stopped`. On a
shared or desktop machine that starves every other process; RandomX also
allocates roughly 2 MB of scratchpad per thread plus a 2 GB dataset, which on a
small host is an OOM.

## Fix

Constrain the Compose service to match the documented Kubernetes shape, and let
users raise it deliberately:

```yaml
  xmrig:
    image: ivuorinen/docker-xmrig:latest
    volumes:
      - ./config.json:/etc/xmrig/config.json:ro
      - ./log:/log:rw
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 2G
```

and add a README line stating that the default is one core and how to raise it.

## Resolution
Added deploy.resources.limits (cpus 1, memory 2G) to the compose service, matching deployment.yaml. Verified with 'docker compose config'. README states the default and that it should be raised deliberately.
title: Compose file sets no CPU or memory limits; the miner saturates every core on the host by default

body:
## Problem

xmrig is configured to write a log file forever, into a location with no
rotation, no size cap, and — because of the mount mismatch — no host volume.

## Evidence

`config.json:32,43-44,48`:

```json
  "log-file": "/log/xmrig.log",
  "print-time": 60,
  "health-print-time": 60,
  "syslog": true,
```

xmrig has no built-in rotation; `log-file` is append-only for the process
lifetime. `Dockerfile:36` creates `/log` inside the image, and no manifest mounts
a volume there — `docker-compose.yml:9` mounts `/xmrig/log` instead, and
`deployment.yaml:41-43` mounts only `/xmrig/etc`. So the file lives in the
container's writable layer.

With `print-time: 60` and `health-print-time: 60`, the miner emits a hashrate
block and a health block every minute, indefinitely, alongside every share-accepted
line. `restart: unless-stopped` (`docker-compose.yml:10`) means the container is
long-lived.

## Impact

The writable layer grows without bound until the Docker storage driver's
filesystem fills, at which point every container on that host fails to write.
There is no alert path — `README.md:84-96` tells users to read logs via
`docker logs`, which reads the Docker JSON log driver, not this file, so the
growing file is invisible in normal operation. On Kubernetes the same file fills
the node's ephemeral storage and gets the pod evicted with a message that does not
name xmrig's log.

## Fix

Drop the file entirely and rely on stdout, which is what both `docker logs` and
`kubectl logs` actually read and what the README already documents:

```json
  "syslog": false,
```

and remove the `"log-file"` key. Container logging is the host's job — the Docker
`json-file` driver takes `max-size`/`max-file`, and Kubernetes rotates node logs.

If a file is genuinely wanted, it must be on a mounted volume with rotation
outside xmrig, and `docker-compose.yml` must gain:

```yaml
    logging:
      driver: json-file
      options: { max-size: "10m", max-file: "3" }
```

## Resolution
Set syslog:false (no syslogd in the container) and added json-file logging with max-size 10m / max-file 3 to compose, capping the stdout path that 'docker logs' actually reads. NOTE: xmrig's own /log/xmrig.log still has no rotation - it is now on a mounted volume rather than the container layer, and the README states plainly that xmrig does not rotate it and the operator must use logrotate or drop the log-file key.
title: Log file has no rotation or size cap; it grows unbounded inside the container's writable layer

body:
## Problem

The Kubernetes manifest gives the scheduler no way to tell a wedged miner from a
healthy one, and no way to know which build it is running.

## Evidence

`deployment.yaml:29-43` — the container spec has no `livenessProbe`, no
`readinessProbe`, no `startupProbe`, and no `imagePullPolicy`. The image is
`ivuorinen/docker-xmrig:latest` (`:30`) with no tag pin and no digest.

Scanner corroboration: checkov `CKV_K8S_8` (liveness), `CKV_K8S_9` (readiness),
`CKV_K8S_14` (image tag should be fixed, not latest), `CKV_K8S_43` (image should
use digest); trivy `KSV-0013`.

`Dockerfile` likewise has no `HEALTHCHECK` — checkov `CKV_DOCKER_2`, trivy
`DS-0026`.

xmrig's failure mode makes this concrete: when the pool is unreachable it retries
`"retries": 5` times with `"retry-pause": 5` (`config.json:46-47`) and then keeps
the process alive. A pod that has lost its pool connection stays `Running` and
`Ready` forever while producing zero hashes.

## Impact

- Silent zero-hashrate pods. Nothing restarts them, nothing reports them.
- `:latest` with the default `imagePullPolicy` (`IfNotPresent` for a non-`latest`
  tag, `Always` for `latest`) means replicas scheduled at different times can run
  different builds of the same "version", and a rollback is impossible because
  there is no immutable reference to roll back to.

## Fix

Pin the image and add a liveness probe that fails when the miner is not connected.
xmrig exposes an HTTP API for exactly this; enable it in `config.json`:

```json
  "http": { "enabled": true, "host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 8080, "restricted": true },
```

then in `deployment.yaml`:

```yaml
        - image: ivuorinen/docker-xmrig:6.22.2
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: { path: /2/summary, port: 8080 }
            initialDelaySeconds: 60
            periodSeconds: 30
```

Prefer a digest (`ivuorinen/docker-xmrig@sha256:...`) if reproducible rollout
matters; Renovate already manages digest pins elsewhere in this repo.

## Resolution
Added liveness and readiness httpGet probes on the xmrig HTTP API (enabled restricted/read-only in config.json) plus imagePullPolicy: Always and a HEALTHCHECK in the Dockerfile. Verified the endpoint serves /2/summary and docker reports health=healthy. TWO RESIDUALS, both deliberate: (1) the probes do not detect a disconnected pool - testing showed the API answers normally at zero hashrate - and wiring pool state into liveness would turn a pool outage into a crashloop, so it is left out and a separate finding tracks the gap; (2) the manifest still references :latest, which is correct for a reference manifest in the image's own repo, now carrying an explicit comment and a README step telling operators to pin.
title: Deployment has no probes, no imagePullPolicy, and floats on :latest with no digest

body:
## Problem

The documented remedy for log-directory permissions is world-writable mode 0777.

## Evidence

`README.md:108-112`:

> And give full permissions to the directory on the host machine:
>
> ```bash
> chmod 777 "$(pwd)"/log
> ```

## Impact

Every local user and every other container that bind-mounts the same path can
read, modify, and delete the miner's logs, and can plant files there. On a shared
host that is a tamper channel for the only forensic record the deployment keeps.
The advice is also unnecessary: the container currently runs as root
(see the root-container finding), so it can already write any directory — 0777
solves a problem that does not exist today, and will solve the wrong problem once
a non-root `USER` is added.

## Fix

Replace the `chmod 777` block with ownership matching the container's uid. Once
the Dockerfile gains `USER 10001`:

```bash
mkdir -p "$(pwd)"/log
sudo chown 10001 "$(pwd)"/log
```

For Kubernetes, `securityContext.fsGroup: 10001` on the pod handles the same thing
for a mounted volume, with no host command at all.

## Resolution
Replaced 'chmod 777' with 'sudo chown 10001', matching the image's new non-root uid; Kubernetes side uses securityContext.fsGroup: 10001 instead of a host command.
title: README instructs users to chmod 777 the log directory

body:
## Problem

Three small pieces of the build do nothing or work against the build.

## Evidence

1. `Dockerfile:34-35`:
   ```dockerfile
   RUN apk --no-cache add libuv hwloc gcompat && \
     rm -rf /var/cache/apk/* && \
   ```
   `--no-cache` already means apk never populates `/var/cache/apk`. The `rm -rf`
   removes an empty directory. It is a no-op carried over from the pre-`--no-cache`
   idiom.

2. `gcompat` is installed in both stages (`:8` and `:34`). It is a glibc
   compatibility shim for running glibc-linked binaries on musl. xmrig here is
   compiled from source *on* Alpine against musl (`:19`), so nothing in the image
   needs it. It is vestigial from the Ubuntu-based image this repo used before
   commit `f8e9a10 "feat: switch to alpine 3.20"`.

3. There is no `.dockerignore`. The build context (`context: .` in
   `.github/workflows/build.yaml:56`) therefore includes `.git` — 55 commits of
   history — plus `log/`, `README.md`, `deployment.yaml`, and `docker-compose.yml`.
   Only `config.json` is ever copied (`Dockerfile:39`).

## Impact

Minor but real: a wasted layer instruction, an unnecessary runtime package
(and its CVE surface) in the published image, and every build uploading the git
history to the builder — for both matrix platforms, on every release.

## Fix

```dockerfile
RUN apk --no-cache add libuv hwloc && \
  mkdir -p /etc/xmrig /log
```

and drop `gcompat` from line 8 as well. Add `.dockerignore`:

```
.git
.github
log
*.md
*.yml
*.yaml
```

If `gcompat` turns out to be required, that is worth a comment on the line saying
which binary needs it — right now nothing records why it is there.

## Resolution
Dropped the no-op 'rm -rf /var/cache/apk/*' and removed gcompat from both stages; added .dockerignore excluding .git/.github/log/docs/markdown/manifests. Verified the image still builds and runs without gcompat.
title: Dead and redundant instructions: no-op cache purge, unused gcompat, missing .dockerignore

body:
## Problem

Several README statements describe a repository state that does not exist.

## Evidence

1. `README.md:73`:
   > `replicas`: number of desired pods to be running. As I run a 3 worker node
   > Turing Pi cluster, I run 3 replica's

   `deployment.yaml:9` sets `replicas: 1`.

2. `README.md:25-28` tells the user to set `user: your-miner-identifier`.
   `config.json:38` ships `"user": "${HOSTNAME}"`, which xmrig expands to the
   container hostname (`src/base/io/Env.cpp:62-64`). The README never mentions
   that a working default is already in place, or that it transmits the hostname.

3. `README.md:68-69` claims that without editing, "it will mine against my
   anonymised docker wallet". It cannot — the pool host is unresolvable
   (see the `tunkki:3333` finding).

4. `README.md:81`: `kubectl -f apply deployment.yaml` — the flag and subcommand
   are transposed. The correct form is `kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml`.
   Copy-pasting the documented line produces `error: unknown command "-f"`.

5. `deployment.yaml:13` carries `strategy: {}`, a `kubectl create --dry-run -o yaml`
   artifact. It is inert but signals the manifest was generated and never reviewed
   — consistent with the broken `command:`/`args:` paths in the same file.

## Impact

Item 4 is a copy-paste failure for every user following the Kubernetes path.
Items 1–3 send users looking for behaviour the repo does not have. Because the
README is also pushed as the Docker Hub description
(`.github/workflows/build.yaml:113-118`), these are the public docs for the image.

## Fix

Fix `README.md:81` to `kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml`. Align 1 and 3 with the
manifests (or vice versa). For 2, state that the default worker id is the
container hostname and that it is sent to the pool. Delete `strategy: {}` from
`deployment.yaml:13`.

## Resolution
Fixed 'kubectl -f apply' -> 'kubectl apply -f'; removed the 3-replicas claim contradicting replicas:1; documented that the user field already defaults to ${HOSTNAME}; removed the false default-mining claim; deleted 'strategy: {}' from deployment.yaml.
title: README contradicts the manifests it documents: replica count, config-edit instructions, and default-mining behaviour

body:
## Problem

The default worker identifier sent to the pool is the machine hostname, and
nothing tells the user this.

## Evidence

`config.json:38`: `"user": "${HOSTNAME}"`.

xmrig expands this — `src/base/io/Env.cpp:62-64` registers `HOSTNAME` as a
built-in variable falling back to `gethostname()` when the env var is unset:

```cpp
    String hostname = "HOSTNAME";
    if (!getenv(hostname)) {
        variables.insert({ std::move(hostname), Env::hostname() });
    }
```

Under Docker the container hostname defaults to the container ID (opaque), but
`docker-compose.yml:4` sets `container_name: xmrig`, and Kubernetes sets the pod
name. Users who set `hostname:` or run with `--network host` leak the real host
name.

The connection is plaintext: `config.json:49-51` sets `"tls": {"enabled": false}`,
so the value is visible to anything on the path, not only to the pool.

## Impact

Low in the default configuration and by design for pool identification, but it is
a fingerprint sent to a third party over an unencrypted channel, and
`README.md:25-28` describes the `user` field without mentioning that a hostname
default is already active. A user who deploys without editing the config assumes
nothing identifying is being sent.

## Fix

Document it in the README's Step 2 list: "`user`: your miner identifier. The
shipped config defaults to `${HOSTNAME}`, which xmrig expands to the container
hostname and sends to the pool in cleartext — set an explicit value if you do not
want that." Enable `"tls": {"enabled": true}` when the pool supports it.

## Resolution
README Step 2 now states that user defaults to ${HOSTNAME}, that xmrig expands it to the container hostname, and that it is sent to the pool in cleartext, with a pointer to set an explicit value or enable tls.
title: Container hostname is transmitted to a third-party mining pool by default, undocumented

body:
## Problem

The job that publishes the Docker Hub description cannot fail the workflow.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/build.yaml:105-118`:

```yaml
  update_description:
    if: ${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: true
```

Any failure — expired `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`, a Docker Hub API change, the action
being renamed — is swallowed. The workflow reports green.

## Impact

The Docker Hub description silently stops tracking the README. Given that the
README is the only user-facing documentation for the image and currently contains
a `docker run` command that cannot work, a stale-but-green description is exactly
the failure that keeps a broken quickstart published. Nothing surfaces the
divergence.

## Fix

Remove `continue-on-error: true`. If the intent was that a description failure
should not invalidate an already-published image, that is already true — the
`merge` job has completed and pushed by the time this job runs, and a failed job
does not unpublish anything. Letting it go red is the point: it is the only signal
that the docs are out of sync.

## Resolution
Removed 'continue-on-error: true' from update_description so a failed description push fails the workflow.
title: update_description job masks its own failures with continue-on-error

body:
## Problem

Two small Compose defects in the reference manifest.

## Evidence

`docker-compose.yml:4`: `container_name: xmrig` — setting an explicit container
name makes `docker compose up --scale xmrig=N` fail for any N > 1 with
`"cannot create container: conflict, the name is already in use"`. The service
name `xmrig` (`:2`) already gives a predictable DNS name and a predictable
`docker compose logs xmrig`, so the explicit name buys nothing.

`docker-compose.yml:11-14`: the `watchtower` service has no `restart:` policy,
while `xmrig` has `restart: unless-stopped` (`:10`). An auto-updater that stops
on the first transient Docker Hub error and never comes back is worse than no
auto-updater: the operator believes updates are happening when they stopped
weeks ago.

## Impact

Scaling the miner across cores or hosts with Compose requires editing the file
first. The watchtower asymmetry produces a silently dead update path — relevant
only if the watchtower service survives the separate finding recommending its
removal.

## Fix

Delete line 4. If watchtower stays, give it `restart: unless-stopped` to match.

## Resolution
Removed 'container_name: xmrig' so the service can scale; the watchtower restart-policy half is moot because watchtower was removed entirely.
title: container_name pins the service to a single instance and watchtower has no restart policy
